title: Students ask for the labels they need most: two orders measured, neither passed, and taught labels kept out of every estimate
request: Phase 7 (the owner): a student behind every choice; 29.11 ranks the label queue by what a label would teach and measures it against labels drawn at random.
plan: Measure on the generated sets: 200 labels asked for against 200 at random, the same seeds and student, the gate fixed before the run.
Offer the order in the product without letting it touch the fair sample a promotion reads.

decisions.decision: After the first rule failed, one second rule, its gate fixed before its run, said as a second attempt; then stop.
decisions.why: A third rule judged on the same dev rows would be fishing: two pre-registered attempts and their failures are the honest result.

decisions.decision: The product offers the second rule as a person's choice, never the default, said as not passed.
decisions.why: It taught more where the student had room (split.strategy, 5 of 5 seeds) and did no harm worth a gate elsewhere, but it did not pass.

decisions.decision: A label chosen to teach is a blind label without a weight: it trains, and never estimates.
decisions.why: Labels chosen by what they teach are not a sample: an accuracy read from them is the student's hardest cases, not its rate.

decisions.decision: The teaching order reaches only decisions outside the blind draw and without a truth yet.
decisions.why: A taught label on a drawn decision took it out of the fair sample; on one with a benchmark it displaced a truth an estimate read.

change: dclab_core/active.py (priority, select, select_mixed, split_labels; 0.85.0); dclab_rnd/active_learning.py and evidence/campaigns/active_learning_v1 (ALQ-001, ALQ-002); the queue's teaching order (outside the draw, without a truth, within each point, points in turn); blind_label(taught=True); the measurement, demotion, the Evaluation page and an own student's exam read only labels an estimate may read; the Admin queue's order choice with its honest wording.

findings.defect: The plan's order taught less than random labels.
findings.scenario: ALQ-001: a disagreement first, then the least sure: data.cases_table 0.757 against 0.847, one seed at 0.51.
findings.cause: Choosing disagreements first skewed the labelled set toward one kind of case.
findings.fix: A second rule, half the least sure and half at random (ALQ-002), fixed before its run; it did not pass either and is offered as a choice, never the default.

findings.defect: Taught labels took drawn disagreements out of the fair sample.
findings.scenario: 30 taught labels: 8 drawn disagreements left the fair queue, all among the least sure, and the remaining sample's mean confidence rose.
findings.cause: The teaching order admitted drawn decisions, and the fair queue treats any blind label as done.
findings.fix: The teaching order skips drawn decisions; a taught label on one is refused.

findings.defect: A taught label displaced a truth an estimate read.
findings.scenario: 60 benchmark-labelled records: 20 taught labels moved 9 out of the labelled disagreements; in demotion they could shield a routed model's mistakes.
findings.cause: Blind ranks first in the label rule, and the estimate skipped records whose effective label was taught.
findings.fix: The estimate and demotion choose the truth among labels an estimate may read; the teaching order skips decisions that already have a truth.

findings.defect: The texts claimed more than the measurement.
findings.scenario: Docstrings said the rule was backed and taught as much elsewhere; the page said what teaches most.
findings.cause: Words written before the second result was read closely.
findings.fix: Every text says not passed, with its numbers; the page names the order least sure and random (measured: not passed).

findings.defect: Every point at once compared confidences across points with different numbers of options.
findings.scenario: A choice among many options sits near 0.5 where a yes or no sits near 1.0: the least sure half went to the many-option points.
findings.fix: The order is chosen within each point and the points taken in turn.

findings.defect: The Evaluation page and an own student's exam read taught labels.
findings.scenario: An unweighted blind label weighed 1.0 in the page's accuracy and graded the own model's sealed exam.
findings.cause: Only the measurement and demotion had been taught the rule.
findings.fix: Both read only labels an estimate may read.

findings.defect: The taught flag was read loosely.
findings.scenario: The string false read as true.

findings.defect: The queue panel said the fair sample's terms under the teaching order.
findings.scenario: Random order, counts toward acting: all four untrue for taught labels.
findings.fix: The subtitle follows the order chosen.

findings.defect: The first gate gained a field after its run.
findings.scenario: GATE carries rule: disagree_first; ALQ-001's stored gate does not.
findings.cause: The field was added to tell the two rules apart.
findings.fix: A comment says it was named after ALQ-001 ran.

measurements.name: ALQ-001 (disagreement first)
measurements.gate: active_learning_gate_v1: the asked-for student better by 0.01 on two of three points, worse by more than 0.01 on none
measurements.result: split.strategy 0.537 against 0.537, data.cases_table 0.757 against 0.847, task.framing 0.902 against 0.908
limits: One quick logistic student; invented tables; five seeds over one train pool and one dev set.

measurements.name: ALQ-002 (least sure and random)
measurements.gate: active_learning_gate_v2, the same pass, fixed after ALQ-001 failed and before this run
measurements.result: split.strategy 0.599 against 0.537 (5 of 5 seeds), data.cases_table 0.852 against 0.847, task.framing 0.904 against 0.908
limits: Written after seeing the first rule's results on the same dev rows.

outcome: Neither order the plan or its repair proposed beat random labels on the gate; the product keeps the fair order as its default, offers the better-looking second order as a person's choice with its result said, and never lets a label chosen to teach into an estimate.
lessons: Labels chosen for what they teach are a different kind of label from labels drawn to measure: keep them apart everywhere an estimate is read.
Disagreement-first is what measuring a student needs, not what training it needs.
Stop at the pre-registered attempts: a third rule judged on the same dev set is a search, not a measurement.
risks: Taught labels on decisions outside the draw make the workspace's own students learn from the hardest cases first.
